newsitem.title: USA: Davis says may up Carter-Wallace bid.
newsitem.headline: Davis says may up Carter-Wallace bid.

text.p: Billionaire investor Marvin Davis said on Friday he was committed to negotiate an acquisition of Carter-Wallace Inc at $18 a share but would consider a higher bid "if one can be justified."
Davis responded to a statement earlier Friday in which Carter-Wallace said its majority share holder, CPI Development Corp, had no interest in a deal at $18 a share.
"We reiterate our commitment to negotiate to acquire the company for $18 a share," Davis said in a letter addressed to the Carter-Wallace board and made public by Davis.
"Moreover, as we have previously indicated, we would be willing to offer a higher price if one can be justified," Davis added.
Davis said he thought the Carter-Wallace board had ceded its fiduciary responsibility to CPI Development by allowing it to "dictate" the company's position on the bid.
The board has a fiduciary responsibility to form an independent committee to determine whether the Davis proposal was in the best interest of all the company's shareholders, Davis said in the letter.
"Given the company's lackluster performance, we believe that the board has an enhanced obligation to review all alternatives before rejecting an offer," Davis said.

Wall Street has long viewed Carter-Wallace as an acquistion candidate. Carter-Wallace chairman Henry Hoyt Jr. said at the company's July annual meeting that he had no intention of selling out to another company, despite complaints by some shareholders about its low stock price.

Analysts and stock arbitragers said they thought Davis would have to significantly sweeten his bid in order to capture closely held Carter-Wallace, a health-care products firm with brands including Trojan condoms and Arrid deodorant.
